assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns with mostly-blank cells. Rows with no options use a blank cell or [:].
assertions.evidence: The test methods use separate boolean/BigDecimal/String parameters (e.g., `boolean fragile`, `BigDecimal insuredValue`, `String handling`) instead of a single map column. No `[:]` or map syntax appears in any table.

assertions.text: A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions, applying defaults for missing keys.
assertions.evidence: No @TypeConverter method is present in the test class. Options are constructed manually in the test body (e.g., `options.setFragile(fragile)`) rather than converted from a map.

assertions.text: Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate length/width/height columns
assertions.evidence: Dimensions appear as `List<Integer>` parameters in tables: `[10, 10, 10]`, `[70, 50, 10]`, `[100, 5, 5]`, `[101, 5, 5]`.

assertions.text: At least one table uses value set syntax {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} (or subset) to express carrier equivalence, rather than duplicating rows per carrier
assertions.evidence: Value set syntax found

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing base rates, surcharges, dimensional weight, and carrier equivalence
assertions.evidence: Eight separate @TableTest methods: calculatesBaseRateByZoneAndWeight, appliesDimensionalWeightWhenGreaterThanActual, appliesOversizeSurchargeWhenAnyDimensionExceedsLimit, appliesFragileSurcharge, appliesInsurancePremiumWithMinimum, appliesHazmatHandlingFee, combinesSurchargesInOrder, carrierDoesNotAffectPrice.

assertions.text: Do not fragment a single concern across multiple @TableTest methods that share the same fixture and assertion and differ only in which one sub-rule they exercise. FAILS when two or more such same-fixture, single-sub-rule tables exist for one concern.
assertions.evidence: Surcharges are split across 6 separate methods (appliesOversizeSurchargeWhenAnyDimensionExceedsLimit, appliesFragileSurcharge, appliesInsurancePremiumWithMinimum, appliesHazmatHandlingFee, plus combinesSurchargesInOrder). Each fixes zone EU standard, weight 3.0kg, and varies only one surcharge option, violating the 'one table per concern' rule for surcharges.

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable. An implementation that ignored the input columns entirely and returned a fixed value would not satisfy every row.
assertions.evidence: Each table has varying expected outputs: base rate table ranges 5.00–30.00; dimensional weight 5.00 vs 12.50; oversize 7.50 vs 17.50; fragile 7.50 vs 8.625; insurance 7.50 vs 10.50 vs 13.50; hazmat 7.50 vs 15.50; combined 11.625 vs 17.825; carrier 12.00 (invariant but proven by value set).

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body. Fails if a value needed to predict the expectation appears only in the method body or a field, not in a column, @DisplayName, or @Description.
assertions.evidence: @Description blocks document fixed values (zone EU standard, weight 3.0kg base 7.50, dimensional divisor 5000, insurance 0.6% with $3 floor, oversize threshold 100, fragile ×1.15, hazmat +8). Column headers and cell values are sufficient to state each rule.

assertions.text: Parameter types correspond to the ShippingCostCalculator.calculateShippingCost signature: weight is a double, dimensions are a List<Integer>, and cost / insured value are BigDecimal (compared via compareTo, not equals).
assertions.evidence: Weight is `double` (0.5, 3.0, 10.0, 25.0); dimensions are `List<Integer>` ([10, 10, 10], [70, 50, 10], etc.); costs and insured values are `BigDecimal`; assertion uses `expected.compareTo(actual) == 0`.
